title: Picked up again: the v1 agent was blind
text: Reading the v1 code (Dec 2025) found three silent bugs. (1) The lidar read 0 on every ray: it looked for polygons in env.road, which holds Box2D bodies, so no point was ever 'on the road'. (2) 'Traction' was always 1: wheels have no ground_contact attribute (they keep a set of touched tiles), so the off-track penalty never fired. (3) The +500 finish bonus waited for info['finished_track'], a key CarRacing never sets (it says lap_finished). The agent saw only its speed and compass heading. Scored with CarRacing's own reward on 100 unseen tracks, the v1 best model averages -42.9 (best -7.6) and covers 6.5% of a track.

title: Speed: 99% of a step was drawing a picture nobody looked at
text: CarRacing draws its 96x96 state image inside every step(): 8.0 ms of a 9.4 ms step. Box2D's physics alone is 0.09 ms. Training now skips that drawing (videos still render), and a test checks the world stays bit-identical. The new lidar was chosen by a bake-off of six implementations (pure Python, NumPy, numba, C++, Rust, Go): all bit-identical on 900 poses x 19 rays; numba won (no build step, same source as the reference). A full env step is now ~0.5 ms.

title: v2: new eyes, PPO, the real score
text: New 49-number observation: speed, sideways slip, yaw rate, steer, which wheels are on the road, offset and heading against the centre line, 8 centre-line points up to 40 tiles ahead, and 19 lidar rays that work. Two-axis action (steer; gas or brake). Training reward = CarRacing's own score, so training aims at the metric; stage 1 stops hopeless episodes early (-50). PPO with observation and reward normalisation, time-limit bootstrapping. First run: validation 457 at 0.1 M steps.
